summary: Discovery scoping for a 6-week POC to evaluate open models for clinical summarization and bilingual (EN/ES) entity extraction. Discussed workload sizing (~120 rps peak, 30 rps sustained), success criteria (entity F1 >= 0.88 for English/Spanish, latency P95 < 300ms for short summaries, hallucination tolerance thresholds), shortlist of open-model candidates and benchmarking plan. Action items: share bench template, get traces, run baseline on 13B/70B variants, schedule review.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05 11:00 PT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Li (Redwood SE), Samira Khan (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Elena Morales, Samir Patel, Jules Ng, Rashida Khan, Oliver Yao (ArborBio)

[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey, everyone. Thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side — I'm Ethan, AE. Maya is our SE, will drive the bench. Samira on solutions.
[00:12] Dr. Elena Morales: Hi, thanks. High level we want a short POC to decide which open model we can run in production for clinical note summarization and entity extraction in English and Spanish. Timeline is aggressive—want decision in ~6 weeks.
[00:30] Maya Li: Great, we can do a scoped POC. Quick qual question — what's your current traffic pattern? rps? token lengths?
[00:44] Samir Patel: Sure, current cluster emits about 30 requests per second sustained, peak 120 rps during batch ingest windows. Average prompt length is 150 tokens, responses typically ~80-200 tokens. Monthly tokens ~120M.
[01:05] Ethan Park: Perfect, that gives us sizing. For POC we usually simulate 1x and 3x of your sustained to test autoscale.
[01:18] Jules Ng: Success criteria — for us accuracy matters more than cost for the first phase. We need entity extraction F1 >= 0.88 for EN and >= 0.85 for ES. Also false-positive rate on PHI tagging must be low.
[01:34] Rashida Khan: And clinically, hallucinations are unacceptable when there's a diagnosis assertion. We need a threshold — maybe <2% critical hallucination rate on the eval set.
[01:46] Maya Li: Good constraints. We'll build specific evals for hallucination detection and calibration.
[01:53] Ethan Park: Model shortlist idea — we've pulled a few open models that in our experience balance multilingual and clinical language: LLaMA-2 13B (quant), LLaMA-2 70B (full / int8), Mistral-7B-Instruct, Falcon-40B-Instruct. We'll also test a Redwood-optimized 13B quant variant (note: customer-facing name may be different in notes).
[02:18] Dr. Elena Morales: Quick flag — our Spanish dataset includes Latin American idioms and a lot of clinical abbreviations; some models do poorly on those.
[02:28] Maya Li: Noted. We'll include targeted Spanish prompts and the abbreviations list in the seed set.
[02:34] Samir Patel: How about deployment mode — we prefer Dedicated for throughput predictability, but we need a Private option for PHI. Any difference in bench results between hosted vs dedicated?
[02:47] Ethan Park: Performance is similar across modes; differences come from networking and isolation. For Private we can run the same perf profiles but you'll control the KMS and VPC. We should test both if you want to compare latencies end-to-end.
[03:03] Oliver Yao: Security question — can Redwood support customer-managed KMS, private networking, and do you have SOC2/ISO artifacts?
[03:12] Samira Khan: Yes, we have SOC2 and standard compliance docs — we'll share them. KMS integrations with AWS KMS and HSMs are supported for Private.
[03:23] Jules Ng: Bench specifics — what are the core metrics we'll get? P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, F1 on entity extraction, hallucination rate, and memory/GPU footprint per model.
[03:38] Maya Li: Correct. Also end-to-end latency including request routing and decryption for Private tests if desired. We'll collect GPU utilization and kernel breakdowns — that'll help with quantization tradeoffs.
[03:52] Dr. Elena Morales: For the clinical task: two evals — 1) extract entities and map to normalized codes (ICD10/concept), 2) concise note summarization with hallucination detection. We'll provide labeled subset for scoring.
[04:09] Ethan Park: On model quality tradeoffs — generally larger models (70B) give higher recall and fewer hallucinations, but cost and latency go up. Quantized 13B variants can hit ~85-88% F1 on clean English, but Spanish and domain-specific abbreviations sometimes drop performance by 5-10%.
[04:31] Rashida Khan: That's consistent with our internal tests. We prefer not to compromise on clinical safety. If 13B is below threshold for Spanish, we'll need to consider 70B or a retrieval augmentation layer.
[04:45] Maya Li: We'll include a retrieval-augmented config in the bench matrix — RAG with a small medical-kb vector store to help reduce hallucinations. We'll test both pure LM and RAG variants.
[04:57] Samir Patel: For throughput, do you have guidance on batching and latency SLOs? We need <300ms P95 for short summary calls (sub-200 token responses).
[05:08] Maya Li: With continuous batching on GPU and optimized kernels, 13B quant can meet <300ms P95 at modest batch sizes, but 70B is likely to be closer to 400-800ms depending on hardware and sequence length. We'll capture token-level breakdowns.
[05:28] Ethan Park: Costwise, we'll estimate units per 1M tokens for each model and a projected monthly cost based on your 120M tokens. We'll show Dedicated commit vs hosted consumption math.
[05:40] Jules Ng: Bench timeline — what's reasonable for running the matrix?
[05:44] Maya Li: If you provide traces and the labeled eval set by 2026-08-12, we can run an initial baseline in a week (13B/quant + Mistral), then run 70B and Falcon within the following week. Review call in week 3. Total POC 6 weeks including pilot.
[06:02] Dr. Elena Morales: OK. About multilingual quality — will you do translation+monolingual baseline or native bilingual prompting?
[06:12] Maya Li: We'll do both: bilingual prompting and a translate-then-infer baseline. Some models degrade less with bilingual prompts; others prefer English translation. We'll report per-language F1 and the delta.
[06:24] Samir Patel: Any red flags around model licensing for production? We need to be sure license allows commercial use in our stack.
[06:32] Ethan Park: We'll check each model license and flag any restrictions in the bench report. Redwood keeps a model catalog with license metadata; we'll share it.
[06:40] Rashida Khan: Regarding data retention — for hosted tests can you guarantee no persistent logs of prompts?
[06:47] Samira Khan: Hosted has configurable retention; for PHI we recommend Private with customer-managed retention. We'll include retention settings and dataflow diagrams.
[06:55] Jules Ng: I want to call out an internal success metric: if a model plus RAG hits EN F1 >=0.90 and ES >=0.87 with P95 < 400ms, we'll greenlight a 3-month pilot procurement.
[07:13] Ethan Park: Noted — we'll use that as a gating criterion.
[07:18] [Short silence/background noise]
[07:35] Ethan Park: Walkthrough of benchmark matrix (Maya) — we'll run the following axes: model (LLaMA-2 13B q4, LLaMA-2 70B int8, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Falcon-40B-Instruct, Redwood-13B-quant); augmentation (none, RAG); language mode (EN native, ES native, translate->EN); sequence lengths (short summary 80-200 tokens, long summary 400-800 tokens); load profile (1x sustained, 3x sustained peak).
[08:06] Maya Li: We'll instrument hallucination probes: a set of diagnostic prompts designed to elicit risky assertions, and automated detectors for unsupported facts using a reference KB.
[08:20] Dr. Elena Morales: Can you also include entity normalization accuracy to ICD10/LOINC? That's critical.
[08:27] Maya Li: Yes, we'll measure normalization recall/precision as part of the extraction metric.
[08:32] Samir Patel: For the RAG setup, storage and vector size — we'll need guidance on retention and what indices you recommend.
[08:40] Maya Li: Start small — a 50k doc vector store for the bench seeded with your clinical KB extracts. We'll use FAISS/HNSW and make the retrieval latency contribution explicit.
[08:53] Ethan Park: Pricing notes — we can show Hosted per-token and Dedicated reserved pricing scenarios; for Dedicated you'll get better unit economics at commit, while Private will have platform fees plus infra costs.
[09:05] Oliver Yao: On contractual stuff: we will need a DPA and appendix for security controls, plus a playbook for breach notification. We'll coordinate legal.
[09:15] Samira Khan: We'll share standard DPA and the security pack. We'll also propose a short security Q&A to run with your InfoSec team next week.
[09:25] Ethan Park: Any other blockers?
[09:28] Jules Ng: Budget OK. Main concern is timeline and data prep. We'll prioritize trace export and the labeled eval set.
[09:36] Rashida Khan: We'll redact PII but preserve clinical context in the sample set.
[09:40] Maya Li: Great. We'll create a shared S3 workspace and a minimal ingestion script for you to drop the datasets.
[09:49] Ethan Park: Ramp plan — week 1: dataset handoff + bench template; week 2: baseline runs (13B variants); week 3: 70B + Falcon; week 4: RAG experiments; week 5: consolidation + security review; week 6: final review and recommendation.
[10:10] Dr. Elena Morales: If we need an on-prem package for final pilot, is that supported?
[10:17] Ethan Park: Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem deployments; logistics depend on your infra team. We'll surface requirements in the next doc.
[10:25] Samir Patel: For benchmarking hardware, what do you provision? GPU types?
[10:29] Maya Li: For 13B quant we use A10G or T4-class for representative runs; for 70B we'll use A100/4k-class to approximate performance. We'll report normalized per-GPU metrics.
[10:44] Jules Ng: Ok. Who owns the bench orchestration?
[10:47] Maya Li: Redwood SEs will run the bench with customer-supplied traces; Samir will hand off the traces and confirm the dataset. We'll give you a runbook so you can reproduce runs locally if needed.
[10:58] Ethan Park: Let's recap action items and next steps.
[11:03] Ethan Park: 1) Ethan send benchmark template and example prompts by Friday. 2) Oliver and ArborBio security liaison to confirm gaps. 3) Samir to export traces and provide labeled eval subset. 4) Maya to run baseline and share initial report week after traces.
[11:25] Dr. Elena Morales: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[11:29] Jules Ng: No. Thanks — looking forward to the template.
[11:33] Ethan Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the artifacts and schedule.
[11:38] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had occasional name errors (Oliver Yao sometimes tagged as "Oliver Yo"), and some medical abbreviations were mis-transcribed (e.g., "SOB" became "sob"). We preserved original speaker labels from the export where present.
